story: DARPA now has AI-controlled F-16s working as a team in virtual dogfights
text: > What puzzles me is that as of yet, there doesn't seem to be any talk of using "AI" (ie Neural Net stuff) for planning and strategy, which seems like a MUCH more powerful application than this stuff. It'll probably be so effective, it'll still be fighting long after all of humanity has destroyed itself and left an irradiated environment. Here are two science fiction short videos of an artist depicting such a future: "LAST DAY OF WAR" - by Dima Fedotov | TheCGBros - [LINK] "Fortress/Крепость" - by Dima Fedotof | TheCGBros - [VIDEO] (edit: typofix)

story: Geoffrey Hinton leaves Google and can now speak freely about his AI concern
text: identify a target decide to attack the target implement the attack determine the result of the attack If humans are required for the decision, then humans have an inherent hook to prevent more attacks. Otherwise you run into scenarios like [VIDEO] where humans are incapacitated and AI just continue on like nothing has happened. It makes the failure modes more sane. It's not a catch-all but a good agreeable step to take.
